findings.issue: Initial implementation stashed the resolved subscriber/bot on singleton instance fields (driveSubscriber/driveBot) to hand off from preStepGates to drive. The engine is a singleton; runExecution (sweep thread) and resumeOnCallback (Task 5 webhook worker thread) run on different threads concurrently, so the shared mutable fields could cross-talk and send to the wrong subscriber/bot.
findings.suggestion: Pass the resolved (subscriber, bot) by value. Fixed pre-commit: introduced a private record StepContext returned by preStepGates and threaded as a drive(...) parameter, so the singleton holds no per-execution state.

findings.issue: Timeout-resume seam treats a broken cursor (menuStep == null) identically to 'no timeout target' -> complete(). The broken-cursor edge case elsewhere is terminate(failed)+marker. On a timeout, the cursor was just resolved at park time, so a dangling cursor here is only reachable via snapshot corruption; completing is a safe terminal state.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable: completing on timeout when the menu cannot be resolved is a benign terminal outcome and avoids a confusing 'failed' for a run that already sent its menu. Left as-is by design; documented in code comment.

findings.issue: indexOfStep uses reference-identity (==) to locate the current step in the snapshot for default-next resolution.
findings.suggestion: Correct in context: the step always comes from currentStep(exec), which returns the live snapshot element, so identity holds. Private method, single caller. No change.

notes: 11 dimensions reviewed. At-most-once invariant preserved: every state write (persistProgress/scheduleDelay/parkForReply/complete/terminate) is a stillClaimed CAS by _id+stepRunStatus (NOT by index); claimForCallback is scoped by subscriberId (anti-IDOR). Lowercase .name() literals throughout. No PII in logs (ids/codes only). Observability log constants added. waiting_for_reply $in literals verified present in sweep/claim (added by Task 1).
